verses.text: Six days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and his brother John with him up a high mountain, where they were alone.
He was transformed in front of them. His face shone like the sun, and his clothes became as bright as light.
Suddenly Moses and Elijah appeared, talking with him.
Peter said to Jesus, “Lord, it’s good that we’re here. If you want, I’ll set up three shelters—one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
While Peter was still speaking, a bright cloud covered them. A voice from the cloud said, “This is my beloved Son. I’m pleased with him. Listen to him.”
When the disciples heard this, they fell facedown and were terrified.
Jesus came over, touched them, and said, “Get up. Don’t be afraid.”
When they looked up, they saw no one except Jesus.
As they came down the mountain, Jesus instructed them, “Don’t tell anyone what you saw until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead.”
The disciples asked him, “Then why do the scribes say Elijah must come first?”
Jesus answered, “Elijah does come first and will restore everything.
But I tell you, Elijah has already come, and people didn’t recognize him. They did whatever they wanted to him. The Son of Man will suffer at their hands too.”
Then the disciples understood he was talking about John the Baptist.
When they came back to the crowd, a man knelt in front of Jesus and said,
“Lord, have mercy on my son. He has seizures and suffers terribly. He often falls into the fire or into the water.
I brought him to your disciples, but they couldn’t heal him.”
Jesus answered, “You faithless and corrupt generation! How long must I stay with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy here to me.”
Jesus rebuked the demon, and it came out of the boy. The boy was healed at that very moment.
Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and asked, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”

He told them, “Because you don’t believe enough. I’m telling you the truth: if your faith is even as small as a mustard seed, you can tell this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you.
But this kind comes out only through prayer and fasting.”
While they were together in Galilee, Jesus told them, “The Son of Man is about to be handed over to people.
They’ll kill him, and he’ll be raised on the third day.” The disciples were deeply upset.
When they came to Capernaum, the collectors of the two-drachma temple tax came to Peter and asked, “Doesn’t your teacher pay the temple tax?”
“He does,” Peter replied. When he went into the house, Jesus spoke first: “What do you think, Simon? From whom do earthly kings collect taxes and duties—from their own children or from others?”
Peter answered, “From others.” Jesus said, “Then the children are exempt.
But so we don’t cause them offense, go to the sea and cast a hook. Take the first fish you catch and open its mouth. You’ll find a stater coin. Take it and give it to them for me and you.”
